page.layout: One page of text, verse set in italic; no margin notes except the catchword "Quos" at the lower right below the last line.

p.i: Aureos prius indicare ramos: Nec tentare Magi furentes artes, Vt cernas Erebi latentis antro Vmbras lucidulis volare pennis. Hic non Phidiaca manu toreuma Caelatum nitet, aut imago ludit, Qualem vel speculi remittit aequor, Vel fingit placida quiete somnus, Vel pictor varia figurat arte. Hic non illicitis manere iussus Python carminibus struit dolosas Sortes, Tartareove fallit astu. Hic veri Culicis nitente gemma Veras reliquias vides sepultas, Qui quondam Heliadum fluente rore Vnaque implicitus repente gutta, Vi scoso riguit gelu peremptus. Huius magna Themis necem cruentam Et casus subitos miserta iussit Vt quae lachryma saevior necarat Illi perpetuum foret sepulchrum: Quale non Pharijs vetusta fecit Ægyptius Ducibus: vel ipsa Garis charis Artemisia manibus mariti: Cedat Pyramidum labor superbus, Et quae splendida nunc premunt sepultos Reges marmora: quos nefas videre, Quos tempus, caries, situsque perdit:

page.notes: Line "Ægyptius Ducibus: vel ipsa Garis charis": "Garis" is struck through in the print and "charis" is set above or beside it as a correction; both are transcribed as printed, but the struck word is uncertain. The verse is set in italic throughout, lines run on as one stanza with no printed stanza break. Faint show-through from the reverse page is ignored. The bottom-right "Quos" is the catchword.
